turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Good morning, Mrs. Wilson. Before we begin, can you hear me clearly?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Mostly, yes. Sometimes I have trouble when people speak too quickly.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Of course. Tell me what’s been troubling you.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I’ve been feeling this pressure in my chest since yesterday. At first, I thought it was just indigestion.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Can you describe what it feels like? Is it sharp, burning, or more like heaviness?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: More like someone is sitting on my chest. It reminds me of what my husband experienced before his heart attack. I’m frightened something similar might happen to me.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: I understand why that would worry you. We need to take chest pressure seriously. Does it get worse when you walk or climb stairs?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Yes. Yesterday, I had to stop halfway up the stairs because of it.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Have you noticed any shortness of breath when that happens?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: A little, yes. I thought it was just my age.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Have you felt faint, dizzy, or lightheaded with it?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: A little dizzy this morning, but I didn’t faint.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Have you ever been told you have high blood pressure, high cholesterol, or diabetes?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I take tablets for my blood pressure. I don’t have diabetes, as far as I know.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: I’m checking your medical history now. Have you ever had any heart-related procedures?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No, I don’t think so. I’ve never had heart surgery.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Thank you. Your record mentions a heart procedure a few years ago, so we’ll need to verify those details.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I don’t remember that. My daughter usually keeps track of those things.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Given your symptoms, I don’t want to delay evaluation. We need an ECG and an urgent assessment at the emergency department. I’ll arrange for the team to help with your transfer.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I’m sorry, I didn’t catch the last part. What did you say about where I’m going?

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: I’m going to contact the team now so they can get everything ready.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Will my daughter be able to come with me? I get confused when there’s too much information.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: I’ll get the arrangements started. Please stay seated while we coordinate your care.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Okay, thank you.
